Two NET-NEW findings below.

evidence: ppt-web reads the API base URL from TWO DIFFERENT, uncoordinated Vite env variables. Group A uses `VITE_API_URL`: lib/api.ts:77 `const DEFAULT_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'` (the shared axios client), main.tsx:19 `baseUrl: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || ''` (the generated @ppt/api-client OpenAPI.BASE), and features/accounting/api/paymentMatching.ts:69 `${import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || ''}/api/v1/...`. Group B uses `VITE_API_BASE_URL`: contexts/AuthContext.tsx:97 `const API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? ''` (base for createAuthApi -> login/refresh/logout/SSO), plus features/auth/authApiClient.ts:10, features/buildings/hooks/useBuildings.ts:19, features/messaging/hooks/useMessaging.ts:38, features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:15, features/registry/pages/RegistryRulesPage.tsx:14, features/privacy/gdprClient.ts:9, features/neighbors/hooks/useNeighbors.ts:31.

Only ONE of the two names is declared in the typed env surface: vite-env.d.ts:4 declares `readonly VITE_API_URL: string` inside ImportMetaEnv; `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is NOT declared there, so it is untyped (`import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL` is `any`/undefined at the type level) and typos or a missing value are invisible to `pnpm typecheck`. The vite.config.ts comments (lines 34-35) reference BOTH names ('OpenAPI.BASE = '' and VITE_API_BASE_URL = ''' ... 'In production VITE_API_URL must be set explicitly'), confirming the two names are conflated rather than a deliberate split.

Production impact: the api.ts doc-comment (line 76) and vite.config.ts (line 35) both state 'In production VITE_API_URL must be set' — i.e. the documented/typed knob is VITE_API_URL. In a cross-origin deployment where an operator sets only VITE_API_URL (the documented, typed one), Group B falls back to '' (same-origin relative). That routes the ENTIRE auth flow (login/refresh/logout/SSO callback via AuthContext.getAuthApi) plus buildings, messaging, registry, privacy/GDPR and neighbors requests to the WEB origin instead of the API origin — login and those features break in prod while the axios client + generated api-client (Group A) work, a confusing partial outage. The mirror failure (only VITE_API_BASE_URL set) breaks the axios client and generated client instead.

This is NET-NEW vs prior ppt-web-core signals: none of the mined findings (auth-guard 09-20, authed-roots-adhoc-guard-gap 09-23, fetch-no-auth 09-24, mutation/query error-handling 09-25, errorhandler-raw-message 09-20) touch env-var/base-URL wiring.

Fix (low-risk): consolidate on a single canonical name (VITE_API_URL, since it is the typed + documented one), replace all VITE_API_BASE_URL reads with it (or add a shared `const API_BASE_URL` in one module that both groups import), and declare the canonical name in vite-env.d.ts so a missing value is a type/lint signal. Confidence medium: the two-name divergence and the single-name typing are objectively confirmed by static read; the prod breakage is conditional on deploy-time config that this static pass cannot observe.

features/notification-analytics/hooks/useNotificationAnalytics.ts:64-70 defines useNotificationAnalytics as a bare useQuery with NO `enabled` gate (queryKey + queryFn: () => fetchAnalytics(filters) + staleTime only). It therefore fires on every mount regardless of role or auth state.

routes/groups/notifications.tsx:30-57 NotificationAnalyticsPageRoute calls useNotificationAnalytics(filters) unconditionally, then computes `isOperator = isManagerRole(user?.role)` and passes `data={isOperator ? data : undefined}` (:46) — i.e. for a non-operator the fetched result is explicitly DISCARDED. So every non-operator mount emits an analytics request that the backend answers with 403 (the handler enforces `audit_read`, see the :38-41 comment) and whose payload is thrown away: a guaranteed-forbidden, guaranteed-wasted round-trip on each mount.

The route is also NOT wrapped in <ProtectedRoute> (notifications.tsx:165 `<Route path="/notifications/analytics" element={<NotificationAnalyticsPageRoute />} />`) while its SIBLING in the same file IS (:166-173 `/notifications/triggers` is wrapped). Consequence for an unauthenticated deep-link to /notifications/analytics: no ProtectedRoute redirect fires; instead the ungated query runs with no token -> 401 -> the global axios onUnauthorized handler (AuthContext.handleUnauthorized) runs logout()+redirect. The user reaches /login, but via the failed-request/global-logout path rather than the clean setReturnUrl redirect that ProtectedRoute performs for every other operator route. In the nav the link is already operator-gated (App.tsx:148-152 `isOperator && <Link to="/notifications/analytics">`), confirming the intended gating that the route level omits.

Distinct from the 2026-09-20 routes-missing-auth-guard finding, which enumerated faults/announcements/disputes/messaging/neighbors/community and did NOT include notifications.tsx; and the fresh mechanism here (a useQuery with no `enabled` firing a request whose result is discarded for non-operators) is not covered by any prior signal.

Fix (low-risk): gate the hook with `enabled: isOperator` (pass isOperator into useNotificationAnalytics, or lift the enabled flag), and wrap the route in <ProtectedRoute requiredRoles={MANAGER_ROLES}> to match the sibling and the nav gating. Confidence medium: the missing `enabled` and the missing wrapper are confirmed by static read; the exact 403/401 runtime sequence is inferred from the handler comments and the shared axios 401 path, not runtime-confirmed.
